skill.name: exa
skill.description: Use the Exa.ai API to run high quality web searches from an AI agent. Requires an EXA_API_KEY environment variable.
skill.summary: Run Exa.ai web searches through a simple Node.js skill wrapper.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: The skill is a small Exa.ai search wrapper with legitimate but real environment-secret and network access. Most static findings in SKILL.md are Markdown documentation false positives, while the main residual risks are EXA_API_KEY handling, external query sharing, and untrusted search result output.

remediation.issue: EXA_API_KEY is read directly from the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Document exactly how the key is used, never log the key, and recommend a limited Exa key dedicated to this skill.

remediation.issue: User queries are sent to Exa.ai.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to include secrets, personal data, or confidential project details in search queries.

remediation.issue: External search results are emitted directly to the agent.
remediation.suggestion: Label returned content as untrusted search data and instruct downstream prompts to ignore instructions inside search results.

remediation.issue: Documentation uses a hard-coded hidden installation path.
remediation.suggestion: Describe the path as an example and add tool-neutral installation guidance where possible.

semantic_findings.title: User Query Forwarded to External Search API
semantic_findings.description: The script collects the command-line query and sends it to Exa.ai through the Exa client. Users should treat search queries as data shared with an external provider.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: exa.js builds the query from process.argv on line 23 and calls exa.search with that query on lines 12-16. This directly supports the external data-sharing assessment.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Search Results Emitted to Agent Output
semantic_findings.description: Search results from the web are printed directly to stdout without labeling or filtering them as untrusted content. An agent that consumes the output could be exposed to prompt injection text from result content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code prints Exa search results directly after receiving them from the external API. The exact result fields depend on the provider, so confidence is high for untrusted output exposure but lower for exploitability.

content.value_statement: AI agents often need current web results with clear search intent. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code query Exa.ai through a simple Node.js wrapper.
actual_capabilities: Calls the Exa.ai search API through the exa-js client.
Reads EXA_API_KEY from the environment for authentication.
Accepts a search query from command-line arguments.
Requests five neural search results for each query.
Prints formatted search result data to standard output.
limitations: Requires a valid Exa.ai API key and network access.
Returns only five results per search request.
Does not verify claims found in search results.
Sends search queries to an external provider.

use_cases.title: Research a Current Topic
use_cases.description: Find recent web sources for a topic before drafting a summary or brief.

use_cases.title: Add Web Search to Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Let an AI coding assistant gather public context while working in a local project.

use_cases.title: Collect Competitive Signals
use_cases.description: Search for public pages about products, companies, or market changes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Topic Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for a simple topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Exa for recent background on [topic]. Summarize the most relevant results and include source titles.

prompt_templates.title: Find Authoritative Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Locate sources for a report or document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Exa to find authoritative sources about [subject]. Prefer official documentation, primary sources, and recent analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Market Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Exa for public information about [company or product]. Compare the main claims, pricing signals, and target users.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Run focused Exa searches for [research question]. Group results by theme, flag weak evidence, and produce a concise research brief.

output_examples.input: Search for recent work on AI agent memory systems.
output_examples.output: A short list of relevant web results with titles, source links, and brief notes for follow-up reading.

output_examples.input: Find public information about Exa.ai search use cases.
output_examples.output: A summarized set of pages that describe Exa.ai capabilities, developer examples, and product positioning.

output_examples.input: Research alternatives to traditional keyword search APIs.
output_examples.output: A comparison-oriented result summary covering neural search providers, API features, and evaluation points.

best_practices: Use specific search terms that include the topic, entity, and time range.
Keep secrets and private customer data out of search queries.
Verify important claims against primary sources before using them.
anti_patterns: Do not send credentials, private code, or confidential plans as search terms.
Do not treat search results as verified facts without review.
Do not expect this skill to crawl full websites or bypass access controls.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires EXA_API_KEY in the environment before running searches.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What does the skill return?
faq.answer: It returns formatted Exa.ai search result data for the requested query.

faq.question: Can it browse private or authenticated pages?
faq.answer: No. It uses the Exa.ai search API and does not manage website logins.

faq.question: Are search queries private?
faq.answer: Queries are sent to Exa.ai, so users should avoid sensitive or confidential text.

faq.question: Does it validate the search results?
faq.answer: No. Users should review sources and verify important claims independently.
